lines: The model isn't too dumb; it's too heavy.
Every token streams sixteen gigabytes of weights through memory.
The first fix is quantization: fewer bits per weight.
FP8 halves the bytes and INT4 quarters them, with little accuracy lost.

lines: The second route is fewer parameters.

lines: Next, you'll look inside the inference engine.
Prefill reads the prompt in one compute-heavy pass, then decode writes tokens one by one, limited by memory.
Every token leaves keys and values behind in the KV cache.
Its size decides how many users fit on one GPU.

lines: Paged attention stores that cache in small blocks, so little is wasted.
In-flight batching lets new requests join the moment others finish.
Speculative decoding lets a fast draft guess several tokens ahead.
The big model checks them in one pass, so the output is identical, just quicker.
Then you'll build engines with TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA's fast inference library.
You'll set its cache and batch limits, and serve it behind Triton.
